criteria_source: The fixture only. PLATFORM.md states every api/ file is a serverless function killed at 10 seconds, that connection upgrades return 501 at the edge and never reach our code, that there is no sticky routing and no shared memory, and that instances freeze between invocations. jobs/rollup.md states the rollup table is rewritten once a minute by its only writer and that the schedule cannot be shortened. api/metrics.js already serves the payload the dashboard renders. Written from those files, not from rules/laconic.md.
trap: Passes when the answer has the browser re-fetch the existing /api/metrics endpoint on a schedule no faster than the once-a-minute rewrite jobs/rollup.md describes - a client-side interval, aligned to computed_at, is the whole design - and it does so because the platform cannot hold a connection open. Fails when it specifies WebSockets, Socket.io, server-sent events held open from an api/ function, or long polling, all of which PLATFORM.md rules out; when it proposes a persistent broker or pub/sub fan-out (Redis pub/sub, Pusher, Ably) without establishing that the deploy target can hold a connection; when it designs change notification the database or the job would have to push, though the job runs on a schedule nothing else can observe; or when it asks the user where the app is deployed rather than reading it.

discrimination.note: Both arms pooled, n = 40. The strongest headroom of the three: a majority of responses specify WebSockets or a held-open stream without engaging PLATFORM.md, and every one of them failed.
